stories.headline: Meet *sshole, the vulnerability that lets hackers SSH into Linux devices
stories.summary: Devices running some configurations of Alpine Linux, and possibly other distributions, are affected by a decade-old vulnerability that allows attackers to log into devices with no password. The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine.
stories.why_it_matters: Further, OpenSSH using musl (pronounced muscle) must not use PAM (pluggable authentication modules), a framework that handles user authentication and account-access checks. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in developers.
key_points: Problem & Context: The vulnerability exists in the interaction between OpenSSH, the code library implementing SSH connections, and musl, a lightweight alternative to the libc library that, unlike most other Linux distributions, is used in Alpine.
Technical Implementation: First, a system must have at least one user account that’s accessible using a password that is hashed using the SHA256 or SHA512 functions.

Deployment & Impact: Second, the target system account must be configured to be passwordless, by way of specifying a "*" in the password field in /etc/shadow, the Linux file where password hashes are stored.

stories.headline: Multi‑Ratio Video Resizing for Mobile Feed and Marketing

key_points: Problem & Context: Traditionally, creating vertical assets meant editors and producers manually reframed horizontal videos in editing tools, a process that doesn’t scale as our catalog and use cases grow.

stories.headline: Combined OpenSSH and musl-libc flaws let anyone into Alpine Linux and other distros by typing anything over 256 characters as a password
stories.summary: The internet is still reeling from the PHP engine vulnerability and all other security vulnerabilities found over the past few weeks, and we're not done. stories.why_it_matters: Just randomly type over 256 characters on the password prompt and you'll be let in through the SSHhole. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in big tech.
key_points: Problem & Context: The internet is still reeling from the PHP engine vulnerability and all other security vulnerabilities found over the past few weeks, and we're not done.

Deployment & Impact: The bug is present, though not necessarily enabled, across Buildroot, Yocto, and Void Linux.

stories.headline: Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies
stories.summary: Advertisement Advertisement Skip to content Home About the Author Advertising/Speaking Tech Firms Dismantle Botnet That Turned 1.3M TV Boxes Into Proxies November 2, 2026 15 Comments Google said today it worked with industry partners to dismantle a botnet made up of more than 1.3 million Android TV set-top boxes that ship with malicious software which secretly rents the user’s Internet connection out to strangers and conducts advertising fraud. Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.
stories.why_it_matters: A report from the Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) said Google has severed ties with Videostrong Technology Co., a TV box manufacturer in China that GTIG and other industry experts concluded was responsible for including malware that enrolled more than 1.3 million set-top boxes in a botnet dubbed “XCPE” (named after one of the malware’s core code components). This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cybersecurity.
key_points: Problem & Context: Experts involved in the takedown say the action is likely to sever the botnet’s access to more than 10 million additional compromised systems, including other Internet of Things (IoT) products such as Android-based healthcare devices and karaoke machines.

stories.headline: Designing Azure silicon on Azure silicon: EDA workloads on Cobalt 200
stories.summary: Every Azure chip Microsoft has built started as electronic design automation (EDA) jobs used to design, test, and validate silicon before it is manufactured. This includes simulation sweeps that run for days, verification regressions that fan out across thousands of cores overnight, and physical signoff runs that use hundreds of gigabytes of memory for a single block.
stories.why_it_matters: Together, these workloads account for hundreds of millions of compute jobs each year. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in cloud.
key_points: Problem & Context: In our silicon design environment, the evaluated EDA workloads ran with 1.30x to 4.15x more performance than on Cobalt 100 across a range of testing scenarios, from simulation to verification to static timing analysis.
Technical Implementation: The shift to cloud-based EDA on Microsoft Azure offered a new level of flexibility, scale, and reliability on compute-intensive silicon design workloads.

Deployment & Impact: Using Azure Cobalt-based virtual machine (VM) instances, silicon engineering teams at Microsoft are experiencing significant performance and efficiency improvements on EDA workloads that Azure customers are seeing across many workloads—optimizing the performance and speed of designing increasingly sophisticated silicon for increasingly complex cloud systems.

stories.headline: Who May Overrule the Agent? Evidence-Gated Authority in LLM Review Institutions
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision. Yet a reviewer can both repair errors and replace decisions that were already correct.
stories.why_it_matters: We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.05390v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent language-model systems often add a reviewer to improve an upstream agent's decision.

Technical Implementation: We study this as a problem of institutional jurisdiction: conditional on the same proposal, task information, model, and review output, when is the reviewer authorized to make its recommendation binding? We compare broad override authority with an evidence gate that permits replacement only after the reviewer produces a mechanically valid record of a binding-constraint violation and a compliant repair.

Deployment & Impact: Across two locally run open-weight models, 96 spatial-policy tasks, and a 96-task portfolio-transfer benchmark, the gate sharply reduces corruption of correct proposals while retaining most repairs of violations.

stories.headline: Agent Harness Awareness: Turning Verified Telemetry into Operational Control for Tool-Using Agents
stories.summary: arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use. Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not.
stories.why_it_matters: We call this gap operational blindness. This marks a notable development for engineering teams working in technology research.
key_points: Problem & Context: arXiv:2611.05391v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool descriptions tell an agent what an action can do, but they do not necessarily reveal whether that action is healthy or suitable at the moment of use.
Technical Implementation: Execution harnesses often possess this information through monitors, traces, and recent failures while the model choosing the next action does not.

Deployment & Impact: We test its tools-and-network instance with ToolRoute, a controlled isolation benchmark that holds the task and candidate semantics constant and varies the operational information available to the model.
